## 結論

**Raycast Extension 現在已不再是 macOS-only。**
Raycast for Windows 已進入公開 Beta，目前支援 **Windows 10 21H2+ 與 Windows 11**；而且可以直接在 Windows 上建立、匯入、測試與 fork Extension。([Raycast][1])

不過要區分：

> **Raycast Extension API 是跨平台設計，但每個 Extension 不一定天然跨平台。**

## 哪些 Extension 幾乎可以直接通用？

這類通常可以共用同一份程式碼：

* 呼叫 REST / GraphQL API
* GitHub、Notion、Linear、Todoist 等 SaaS integration
* 文字處理、JSON formatter、翻譯、搜尋
* 使用 Raycast 的 `List`、`Form`、`Detail`、`ActionPanel`
* 純 TypeScript / React / Node.js 邏輯
* 不依賴 OS 原生 binary 的 npm package

Raycast 官方表示：**不需要 native code 的 Extension，原則上可以直接在 macOS 與 Windows 運作**。Extension 本身使用 React、TypeScript、Node.js，而 UI 由 Raycast host 負責呈現，因此不像一般網站需要自己處理 DOM、CSS 與兩套桌面 UI。([Raycast][1])

只需要在 `package.json` 宣告：

```json
{
  "name": "my-extension",
  "title": "My Extension",
  "platforms": ["macOS", "Windows"],
  "commands": [
    {
      "name": "index",
      "title": "Open Extension",
      "description": "Example command",
      "mode": "view"
    }
  ]
}
```

`platforms` 可設定成：

```json
["macOS"]
```

```json
["Windows"]
```

或：

```json
["macOS", "Windows"]
```

官方文件特別提醒：舊 Extension 若未設定 `platforms`，預設視為：

```json
["macOS"]
```

所以有些 Extension 的程式其實已經能在 Windows 跑，但作者尚未測試及加入 Windows 宣告，它仍然不會出現在 Windows Store 搜尋結果中。Raycast Store 只顯示目前作業系統相容的 Extension。([Raycast Developers][2])

## 哪些情況需要移植？

### 1. 執行系統 script

macOS：

```ts
import { runAppleScript } from "@raycast/utils";
```

Windows：

```ts
import { runPowerShellScript } from "@raycast/utils";
```

`runAppleScript` 只支援 macOS；`runPowerShellScript` 只支援 Windows。([Raycast Developers][3])

可以保留同一個 Extension，將 OS-specific 邏輯隔離：

```ts
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";

if (isWindows) {
  // PowerShell / Windows implementation
} else {
  // AppleScript / macOS implementation
}
```

比較好的目錄結構是：

```text
src/
├── index.tsx
├── platform/
│   ├── macos.ts
│   └── windows.ts
└── shared/
    └── api.ts
```

UI 與商業邏輯共用，只分離系統整合部分。

### 2. 鍵盤快捷鍵不同

不要把 `⌘` 寫死。Raycast 支援 per-platform shortcut：

```ts
const shortcut = {
  macOS: {
    modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"],
    key: "c",
  },
  Windows: {
    modifiers: ["ctrl", "shift"],
    key: "c",
  },
};
```

也可以優先使用 Raycast 的 common shortcuts，由 host 自動映射。官方指出，寫死 `cmd` 的 shortcut 在 Windows 會被忽略，寫死 Windows modifier 在 macOS 也同樣不生效。([Raycast Developers][2])

### 3. 路徑與應用識別方式

例如：

```text
macOS:   /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app
Windows: C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe
```

macOS 應用通常使用：

```ts
application.bundleId
```

Windows 則可能使用：

```ts
application.windowsAppId
```

Raycast 的 `Application` 型別已同時提供 `bundleId` 與 `windowsAppId`。([Raycast Developers][4])

Preference 預設值也可按平台設定：

```json
{
  "name": "workspacePath",
  "type": "textfield",
  "title": "Workspace",
  "default": {
    "macOS": "/Users/me/projects",
    "Windows": "C:\\Users\\me\\projects"
  }
}
```

([Raycast Developers][5])

## 目前仍有一些 Windows 限制

截至目前 Windows 版仍是 Beta，並不是每一項 Extension API 都已對齊 macOS。官方文件目前明確標示：

| 功能/API                          | macOS | Windows |
| ------------------------------- | ----: | ------: |
| 一般 React UI Extension           |     ✅ |       ✅ |
| REST/API integration            |     ✅ |       ✅ |
| Node.js 邏輯                      |     ✅ |       ✅ |
| PowerShell script               |     ❌ |       ✅ |
| AppleScript                     |     ✅ |       ❌ |
| `MenuBarExtra`                  |     ✅ |       ❌ |
| Browser Extension API           |     ✅ |    暫未支援 |
| Extension Window Management API |     ✅ |    暫未支援 |
| AI Extensions                   |     ✅ |    暫未支援 |

([Raycast Developers][6])

這裡有個容易混淆的地方：

* **Raycast 本身的 Windows Window Management 功能**已存在。
* 但第三方 Extension 使用的 **`WindowManagement` API**，官方開發文件目前仍標記為 Windows 不可用。

也就是「內建功能存在」不等於「已開放同等 Extension API」。

## 可以直接在 Windows 開發嗎？

可以。Windows 版早在 2025 年 9 月就加入：

* `Create Extension`
* `Import Extension`
* `Fork Extension`
* 本地開發 stack trace
* 開發與測試流程

基本流程為：

```powershell
winget install raycast
```

準備 Node.js 與 npm，然後在 Raycast 中執行 **Create Extension**。進入產生的目錄：

```powershell
npm install
npm run dev
```

Extension 會在 Raycast 中以 development mode 載入，支援 hot reload 與錯誤顯示。官方目前要求 Node.js 22.14+、npm 7+。([Raycast][7])

## 開發時的建議策略

如果你是自己從零寫，建議一開始就採用：

```json
"platforms": ["macOS", "Windows"]
```

然後遵循三層：

```text
Raycast UI
    ↓ 完全共用
Domain / API logic
    ↓ 儘量共用
OS adapter
    ├── macOS: AppleScript / bundleId / POSIX paths
    └── Windows: PowerShell / windowsAppId / Windows paths
```

這樣一個 Extension 可以做到約：

* **SaaS/API 型 Extension：接近 100% 共用**
* **一般本地 CLI wrapper：約 70–90% 共用**
* **深度 OS automation：約 30–70% 共用**
* **Menu Bar、AppleScript、Finder 深度整合：通常需 macOS-only 或另做 Windows implementation**

所以實際答案是：

> **現在可以在 Windows 使用及開發 Raycast Extension；技術棧本身是跨平台的。純 React/TypeScript/API Extension 通常只需加入 Windows manifest 並測試，涉及 AppleScript、Menu Bar、Finder、原生 binary 或特定 OS API 時，才需要分平台實作。**

5	
6	# Raycast extension development
7	
8	A Raycast extension is a manifest (`package.json`) plus React components, bundled
9	by esbuild and run inside Raycast's own Node 22 process — which launchd starts,
10	so it has none of your shell environment. The API surface is well documented at
11	<https://developers.raycast.com>. Read that for what `List` and `Form` accept.
12	
13	This skill is the other 20%: what the toolchain does **not** check, what the
14	runtime does **not** provide, and what the store checks that the linter does not.
15	Every claim here was paid for once in a shipped extension; the `## Gotchas`
16	section is the compressed bill.
17	
18	macOS only. `platforms`, `sips`, Homebrew prefixes, and launchd are all
19	macOS-shaped, and a `menu-bar` command does not exist anywhere else.
20	
21	## When to use
22	
23	- "Build me a Raycast extension for X" → Workflow A, then B if X is a CLI.
24	- "Wrap this CLI / API in Raycast" → Workflow B. The seam design is the decision
25	  that matters; everything else is recoverable.
26	- "It works in `npm run dev` but not from Raycast" → the launchd PATH gotcha.
27	  This is the most common report and the dev terminal cannot reproduce it.
28	- "The menu bar shows the wrong count / nothing / stale data" → Workflow E.
29	- "My action flashes the new state, reverts, then re-applies" → Workflow C.
30	- "Get this ready for the Raycast Store" → Workflow F and
31	  `scripts/check-store-readiness.sh`.
32	- Reviewing an existing extension: run the gate (Workflow A) first. It usually
33	  finds something, because `ray build` alone never would have.
34	
35	## When NOT to use
36	
37	- **Raycast Script Commands** — shell scripts in a different repo, no manifest,
38	  no React, no `@raycast/api`. Entirely separate surface.
39	- **Generic React/TSX quality** (hook rules, component structure, a11y) → the
40	  `react-best-practices` skill is the better authority. This skill deliberately
41	  restates none of it.
42	- **The semantics of the CLI being wrapped** — `pueue`'s flags, `gh`'s JSON —
43	  belong to that tool's own skill or its `--help`.
44	- **AI Extensions (`tools[]`) when the user has no Raycast Pro.** They are
45	  Pro-gated, so they can never be the primary UX. And there is no `confirmAlert`
46	  equivalent inside a tool call, so a first version must be read-only.
47	- **Taking the store screenshots.** This skill can verify their count and
48	  dimensions. It cannot capture a window, and no CLI can — see Workflow F.
49	
50	## The gate
51	
52	`ray build` — the default `-e dev` build, which is what `npm run build`,
53	`just build`, and `ray develop` all run — proves only that a bundle exists.
54	
55	| Command | Catches | Misses |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| `tsc --noEmit` | types | manifest, formatting, runtime shape |
58	| `node dev-check.js` | your own invariants, wire shapes, generated argv | anything you did not assert |
59	| `ray lint` | manifest schema, icons, ESLint, Prettier, **reserved-shortcut collisions**, and — **only under `CI=true`** — `package-lock.json` registry hosts | types |
60	| `ray build` (`-e dev`) | syntax, that esbuild can bundle it | **types — esbuild strips them without checking** |
61	| `ray build -e dist` | the above **plus types** — it shells out to `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | manifest, formatting |
62	
63	Measured on a scaffold with one genuine `TS2345`: `ray build` exits **0** and
64	prints `ready - built extension successfully`; `ray build -e dist` exits **1**
65	and reports the error. So the dist build is a stronger pre-submit check than it
66	looks — but it is not the build you run all day, which is exactly why the type
67	error survives long enough to ship.
68	
69	All four, in that order, every time:
70	
71	```make
72	typecheck: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
73	verify:    npx tsc --outDir .build/verify --module commonjs --target ES2022 \
74	             --lib ES2023 --esModuleInterop --strict src/lib/dev-check.ts \
75	             && node .build/verify/dev-check.js
76	check: typecheck verify lint build
77	```
78	
79	`assets/Justfile.template` is this, complete, plus a `dist` recipe. Two real bugs
80	shipped past `ray build` in the source extension: a `MutatePromise<GroupMap>`
81	passed where `MutatePromise<State>` was expected (it would have emptied the list
82	on every action), and a `ReactNode`/`JSX.Element` clash. Neither printed a line.
83	
84	## Surface map
85	
86	The complete list of extension entry points. There is nothing else.
87	
88	| Entry point | Manifest | Notes |
89	| --- | --- | --- |
90	| View command | `"mode": "view"` | pushes a view onto the navigation stack |
91	| No-view command | `"mode": "no-view"` | runs and exits; **exports `async function Command(props)`, not a component** |
92	| Menu bar command | `"mode": "menu-bar"` | returns a `MenuBarExtra`. **macOS only** |
93	| AI tools | `"tools": [...]` | invoked by Raycast AI. **Pro-gated** |
94	| Script commands | separate repo | shell scripts, not extensions |
95	
96	**There is no widget API** — no Notification Center, Control Center, or
97	Live-Activity surface. A `menu-bar` command is the only way to show something
98	without opening Raycast, and that constrains the whole design.
99	
100	## Repo layout
101	
102	**The extension IS the repo root.** Not a subdirectory: `ray build`, `develop`,
103	and `lint` all resolve `./package.json` and write `./raycast-env.d.ts` relative
104	to cwd, and `ray publish` copies the extension directory *verbatim* into
105	`extensions/<name>/` of the review PR.
106	
107	```text
108	package.json          the manifest — commands, preferences, arguments
109	raycast-env.d.ts      GENERATED by ray build. Commit it.
110	assets/               extension-icon.png (512x512) + monochrome menu-bar SVG
111	metadata/             3-6 store screenshots at 2000x1250
112	src/<command>.tsx     one file per commands[].name — the names must match
113	src/lib/              shared code
114	src/lib/<backend>/    the transport seam (Workflow B)
115	```
116	
117	Consequence of the verbatim copy: anything else in the root — notes, task lists,
118	a docs site, a `.venv` — rides along into the review PR. Use an allowlist export
119	to a scratch directory if that bothers you; a `.gitignore` will not help, because
120	`publish` copies the directory, not the git index.
121	
122	## Workflow A — scaffold or retrofit
123	
124	```bash
125	bash scripts/new-raycast-extension.sh --dir ./my-ext --name my-ext \
126	  --author <your-raycast-username> --command tasks:view --command menu:menu-bar
127	cd my-ext && npm install
128	npm run build          # this is what GENERATES raycast-env.d.ts
129	just check             # the four-stage gate
130	```
131	
132	For an existing extension, skip the script and copy `assets/Justfile.template`,
133	`assets/tsconfig.json.template`, and `assets/dev-check.ts.template` in. The one
134	non-obvious line is `"include": ["src/**/*", "raycast-env.d.ts"]` — omit it and
135	the generated `Preferences` globals are invisible to `tsc`.
136	
137	Then **open the command from Raycast root search**, not from the `ray develop`
138	console. The console inherits your interactive environment; Raycast does not.
139	Anything environment-dependent that you only tested in the terminal is untested.
140	
141	## Workflow B — wrap a CLI behind a transport seam
142	
143	Model every mutation as a **data union**, never as argv strings:
144	
145	```ts
146	export type Mutation =
147	  | { op: "add"; command: string; group?: string; label?: string }
148	  | { op: "kill"; ids?: number[]; group?: string };
149	
150	export interface Transport {
151	  read(o?: ReadOptions): Promise<State>;
152	  mutate(m: Mutation, o?: Options): Promise<number | void>;
153	}
154	```
155	
156	If `mutate` took a `string[]` of argv, a future socket or HTTP transport would
157	have to parse argv back into intent — that is not a seam, it is a shell.
158	`assets/transport.ts.template` is the skeleton, with the argv builder as a pure
159	function so `dev-check` can assert it without spawning anything.
160	
161	Rules that are not negotiable:
162	
163	- **Resolve an absolute binary path.** Preference first, `existsSync`-validated so
164	  a stale value falls through, then probe **both** `/opt/homebrew/bin` and
165	  `/usr/local/bin`, then `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/bin`.
166	- **`execFile` with an argv array. Never `shell: true`.** Nothing re-parses your
167	  quoting, and a user-supplied command stays one argv element.
168	- **Raise `maxBuffer`.** The 1 MB default turns a large JSON read into a parse
169	  error rather than a clear failure. 64 MB is a reasonable ceiling.
170	- **Set a timeout, and know that `execFile` reports its own timeout as a SIGTERM
171	  kill**, not a distinct code.
172	- **Classify stderr into a discriminated `kind`** — `binary-not-found`,
173	  `daemon-not-running`, `bad-arguments`, `timeout`, `command-failed` — and keep
174	  the full text on the error for a `Detail` fence while the `message` stays one
175	  line for a toast title.
176	- **Strip secret-bearing fields at the parse boundary** (Workflow C explains why).
177	- **Global flags precede the subcommand** for clap-based CLIs.
178	
179	Read `references/runtime-and-subprocess.md` **when** the extension shells out,
180	resolves a path, streams output, or reports `spawn … ENOENT`.
181	
182	## Workflow C — data, cache, and mutations
183	
184	```ts
185	const state = useCachedPromise(
186	  (group: string, account: string) => read({ group, account }),
187	  [group, account],                       // <-- arguments, not closure captures
188	  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: stateAbort },
189	);
190	```
191	
192	- **Everything the fetcher depends on must be an argument.** The argument array
193	  is what keys the cache and triggers refetch. A closed-over variable changes
194	  silently and keeps serving the previous account's data.
195	- **One `abortable` ref per independent read**, or a superseded read cancels an
196	  unrelated in-flight one.
197	- **`execute: false` for conditional fetches**, and `keepPreviousData: false`
198	  when the value is per-selection.
199	- **`useCachedPromise` writes to a disk-backed `Cache`.** Every field of the
200	  resolved value lands on disk in plaintext. Strip environment snapshots, tokens,
201	  and auth headers in the parse function, not at render time.
202	
203	For mutations, the default `mutate()` revalidates on success — which is wrong for
204	any backend that acknowledges before it applies:
205	
206	```ts
207	await state.mutate(run(mutation), {
208	  optimisticUpdate: (data) => predict(data, mutation),
209	  rollbackOnError: true,
210	  shouldRevalidateAfter: false,          // the load-bearing line
211	});
212	setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), FAST_MS);
213	setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), SETTLE_MS);
214	```
215	
216	Measured on one such daemon: ack in ~22 ms, applied ~280 ms later, so the
217	built-in revalidate returned pre-change state and visibly undid the action.
218	`400` and `1500` worked there. **Measure your own backend** — those two numbers
219	are a worked example, not a constant.
220	
221	And an optimistic updater must **return its input unchanged when the outcome is
222	unknowable**. A new server-assigned id, a scheduler decision, a reordering: a
223	wrong prediction flickers exactly like no prediction, and is also wrong.
224	
225	Read `references/data-and-state.md` **when** wiring `useCachedPromise`/`mutate`,
226	when an action reverts and re-applies, or when deciding what to persist and under
227	which key.
228	
229	## Workflow D — failure states as data
230	
231	One descriptor, N renderers. The alternative — an `errorMarkdown()` helper per
232	surface — drifts, and the menu bar cannot render a `List.EmptyView` anyway.
233	
234	```ts
235	export interface ErrorDescriptor {
236	  icon: Image.ImageLike;
237	  title: string;
238	  shortTitle: string;    // a few words — the list column is a third of the window
239	  description: string;   // one line, for List.EmptyView
240	  markdown: string;      // a full page, for Detail
241	  actions: ErrorAction[];// DATA: { id, title, icon, copy? | url? | run? }
242	  structural: boolean;   // is the backend gone, or was this read just flaky?
243	}
244	```
245	
246	`structural` is the decision that matters. `useCachedPromise` keeps serving its
247	last good result when a fetch fails — correct for a flaky read, wrong when the
248	backend is gone, because then the cached list renders a dead system as live.
249	
250	| Situation | Render |
251	| --- | --- |
252	| first read failed, no data | `<List><ErrorEmptyView/></List>` — the whole screen |
253	| structural failure, cached data present | a persistent banner row atop the list |
254	| transient failure | an ordinary toast |
255	
256	Actions stay data so every renderer maps them to its own primitive — `Action` in
257	a panel, a `Clipboard.copy` call in the menu bar.
258	`assets/error-descriptor.tsx.template` has all four renderers.
259	
260	## Workflow E — the menu bar
261	
262	```tsx
263	<MenuBarExtra icon={icon} title={n > 0 ? String(n) : undefined} isLoading={isLoading}>
264	```
265	
266	- **There is no badge API.** The count *is* the `title`, and `undefined` is what
267	  removes it.
268	- **`isLoading` is a contract, not a hint.** Never set: Raycast renders then
269	  immediately unloads. Stuck true: the whole tree re-runs every tick.
270	- **`interval` is manifest-only** — a preference cannot change it, and Raycast
271	  renders its own control. Use `"1m"`; the docs contradict themselves on the floor.
272	- **Background refresh is off by default for store installs.** Until the user runs
273	  the command once, a fresh install shows nothing. Put this at the top of the README.
274	- **Raycast restores the item from a database on restart**, not by re-running the
275	  command, so a stale render survives invisibly. Show an `Updated HH:MM` row.
276	- **`confirmAlert` cannot present here** — it renders in the Raycast window, which
277	  is closed while the menu is open. Destructive items go behind `alternate` (⌥),
278	  and the truly dangerous ones are not offered at all.
279	- **Two identical items at the same level cross their `onAction` handlers.** Prefix
280	  every row with its id.
281	- **Cap the item count.** 400 rows must not become 400 menu items every minute.
282	- **Never return `null` on error** — that removes the item entirely from someone
283	  who deliberately enabled it. Render an error menu instead.
284	- Feedback is `showHUD`, not `showToast`. There is no window.
285	
286	Read `references/menu-bar.md` **when** the extension has or is gaining a
287	`mode: "menu-bar"` command, or the menu bar shows stale data, a wrong count, or
288	nothing at all.
289	
290	## Workflow F — ship to the store
291	
292	```text
293	[ ] author is your REGISTERED Raycast username
294	[ ] license: "MIT" AND an MIT LICENSE file
295	[ ] at least one category; platforms: ["macOS"] if any command is menu-bar
296	[ ] package-lock.json committed — npm ci must work from a clean checkout
297	[ ] assets/extension-icon.png at exactly 512x512, readable light and dark
298	[ ] a monochrome template SVG for the menu bar, tinted at runtime
299	[ ] CHANGELOG.md opening with `## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}`
300	[ ] README covering setup, and any background-refresh default
301	[ ] 3-6 PNGs at exactly 2000x1250 in metadata/
302	[ ] tsc --noEmit, ray lint, and ray build -e dist all clean
303	```
304	
305	Then `bash scripts/check-store-readiness.sh .` — because **`ray lint` exits 0
306	with a completely empty `metadata/`**. Screenshot count and dimensions, icon
307	size, the CHANGELOG placeholder, and a real `author` are review-time
308	requirements the linter never runs.
309	
310	Three steps cannot be automated, and pretending otherwise wastes an afternoon:
311	
312	1. **Screenshots.** Raycast's Window Capture, triggered by a hotkey with
313	   "Save to Metadata" ticked. That option only appears once a `metadata/` folder
314	   exists, so create it (with a README inside) before you start.
315	2. **`ray login`** is a browser OAuth flow.
316	3. **`npx @raycast/api@latest publish`** opens a pull request against
317	   `raycast/extensions`. CI runs, then a human reviews. Days, not seconds.
318	
319	Note `ray build` defaults to `-e dev`. Run `ray build -e dist` at least once
320	before submitting — it is the build the store actually produces.
321	
322	Read `references/store-publishing.md` **when** the user asks to publish or make
323	something store-ready, or when `check-store-readiness.sh` fails and you want the
324	reasoning behind a check.
325	
326	## Available scripts
327	
328	- **`scripts/new-raycast-extension.sh`** — scaffold a gated extension: manifest,
329	  tsconfig, flat ESLint config, Justfile gate, `dev-check` harness, one stub per
330	  command, placeholder icon.
331	  - Flags: `--dir DIR --name NAME [--title T] [--author U]
332	    [--command NAME:MODE[:TITLE]]… [--license SPDX] [--no-verify-harness]
333	    [--dry-run] [--force] [--json] [--help]`
334	  - Exit: `0` written · `1` bad args · `2` target not empty · `3` bundled assets
335	    missing · `4` post-write self-check failed
336	  - Does not run `npm install`. It prints the ordered next steps instead.
337	- **`scripts/check-store-readiness.sh`** — the store preconditions `ray lint`
338	  does not check. JSON array of `{id, status, detail, fix}` on stdout.
339	  - Flags: `[DIR] [--json] [--quiet] [--strict] [--help]`
340	  - Exit: `0` all pass · `1` bad args · `2` not an extension directory · `3` a
341	    required tool is missing (check skipped, **not** passed) · `4` a check failed
342	
343	Deliberately absent, so nobody re-adds them: a wrapper around
344	`tsc && ray lint && ray build` (that is a four-line Justfile recipe, already an
345	asset); a PATH-probe script (it would run in *your* shell — the one environment
346	that hides the bug); a manifest validator (`ray lint` already validates against
347	the published schema, and a copy would drift).
348	
349	## Bundled assets
350	
351	| Asset | Use |
352	| --- | --- |
353	| `Justfile.template` | the four-stage gate, plus the `([ -d node_modules ] \|\| npm install) &&` self-bootstrap every recipe needs, because `ray` ships inside `@raycast/api` |
354	| `tsconfig.json.template` | working config; note `include` must list `raycast-env.d.ts` |

362	
363	## Reference files
364	
365	Load one only when its condition fires. Do not preload.
366	
367	| Reference | Read it **when** |
368	| --- | --- |
369	| `references/runtime-and-subprocess.md` | the extension shells out, resolves a binary path, spawns or streams a subprocess, or reports `spawn … ENOENT` / "works in my terminal but not from Raycast" |
370	| `references/manifest-and-commands.md` | adding or renaming a command, adding preferences or arguments, wiring one command to launch another, or considering AI tools |
371	| `references/data-and-state.md` | wiring `useCachedPromise`/`usePromise`/`mutate`, an action visibly reverts and re-applies, or deciding what to persist and under which key |
372	| `references/ui-patterns.md` | building a List/Detail/Form surface, adding a dropdown or shortcut, rendering program output as markdown, or designing empty and error states |

375	
376	## See also
377	
378	- `react-best-practices` — hooks and component rules. A Raycast extension is
379	  React; this skill covers only what is Raycast-specific.
380	- `verifiable-surfaces` — `--help`/`--dry-run`/exit-code design, if you bundle
381	  helper scripts alongside the extension.
382	- `project-knowledge-harness` — the `pitfalls/` + `backlog/` + `TODO.md` format
383	  the gotchas below were originally recorded in.
384	- `pueue-job-queue` — the CLI the source extension wraps, as an example of what
385	  "the wrapped tool's own skill" means.
386	
387	## Gotchas
388	
389	- **`ray build` does not typecheck in its default `dev` environment.** esbuild
390	  strips types without checking them, so a genuine `TS2345` still prints
391	  `ready - built extension successfully` and exits 0. `ray build -e dist` *does*
392	  typecheck (it runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) — but `npm run build`,
393	  `just build`, and `ray develop` are all the dev build, which is why the error
394	  survives long enough to ship. Keep `tsc --noEmit` in the gate.
395	- **`ray lint` does not typecheck either.** It runs ESLint, Prettier, and manifest
396	  and icon validation. It alone catches reserved-shortcut collisions, so you need
397	  both, and neither is sufficient.
398	- **Raycast runs extensions under launchd, which never sources a shell rc.** `PATH`
399	  is roughly `/usr/bin:/bin`, so a bare `pueue` / `gh` / `uv` fails with
400	  `spawn … ENOENT`. Probe **both** `/opt/homebrew/bin` (Apple Silicon) and
401	  `/usr/local/bin` (Intel) — hardcoding either breaks half of all Macs.
402	- **The dev terminal hides the PATH bug completely.** `ray develop`'s console
403	  inherits your interactive `PATH`, so a resolver that fails in production passes
404	  there. Exercise every environment-dependent change from Raycast root search.
405	- **Starting a daemon *from* Raycast poisons every job it later runs.** The child
406	  inherits Raycast's stripped environment. Only offer a one-click start when a
407	  service manager owns the daemon.
408	- **Never hand-write a `Preferences` or `Arguments` interface.** `ray build`
409	  generates `raycast-env.d.ts` with global `Preferences.<Command>` namespaces
410	  whose fields are *required*; consuming those turns manifest/code drift into a
411	  compile error. Commit it, and regenerate after every manifest edit.
412	- **Raycast has no multi-line preference type.** The allowed set is exactly
413	  `appPicker | checkbox | dropdown | password | textfield | file | directory`;
414	  `"type": "textarea"` fails `ray lint` with `must be equal to one of the allowed
415	  values`. `Form.TextArea` is a form component and unrelated. A "one per line"
416	  setting can only ever hold one entry — pick a single-line separator, and say why
417	  in the docs or a reader will assume it is arbitrary taste.
418	- **Manifest strings have schema minimums, and the error does not name the
419	  field.** `description` ≥ 16 chars, each `commands[].description` ≥ 12,
420	  `preferences[].description` ≥ 8, `tools[].description` ≥ 12. A one-word command
421	  description fails `ray lint` with a bare
422	  `must NOT have fewer than 12 characters` and a line number.
423	- **`useCachedPromise` persists to a disk-backed `Cache`.** Anything in the
424	  resolved value is written to disk in plaintext. One measured payload was 21x
425	  larger with its environment snapshot than without, and that snapshot contained
426	  every secret in the submitting shell.
427	- **Fetcher dependencies must be arguments to the hook, not closure captures.**
428	  The argument array is the cache key. A capture changes silently and keeps
429	  serving the previous account's data.
430	- **`mutate()` revalidates immediately by default, and many backends ack before
431	  they apply.** The follow-up read overwrites the optimistic update with
432	  truth-as-of-a-moment-ago and the action visibly undoes itself. Use
433	  `shouldRevalidateAfter: false` plus two delayed `revalidate()` calls — and
434	  measure your own backend rather than copying anyone's milliseconds.
435	- **An optimistic updater must return its input unchanged when the outcome is
436	  unknowable.** A wrong prediction flickers worse than no prediction.
437	- **Serving cached data on failure is right for flaky reads and wrong for
438	  structural ones.** A cached list renders a dead backend as live, with a toast
439	  that scrolls away as the only hint. Carry a `structural` flag and render a
440	  persistent banner.
441	- **Scope `useCachedState` and `LocalStorage` keys** by whatever the value belongs
442	  to — account, host, workspace. One shared key meant switching machines left a
443	  list filtered by a group that only existed elsewhere, showing nothing.
444	- **A `List.Dropdown` silently resets when its `value` is not among its children.**
445	  Seed a static fallback so the first paint is never empty, and render a synthetic
446	  `(gone)` item for an unknown current value.
447	- **Raycast has taken more shortcuts than `ray lint` knows about.** `⌘K` and
448	  `⌘P` are reserved (Open Action Panel, Open Search Bar Dropdown) and lint fails
449	  on them. But while an extension is *in development* Raycast also injects a
450	  Debug section into every action panel — `⌘R`, `⇧⌘S`, `⇧⌘D`, `⇧⌘X`, `⌘⌥D` —
451	  and **those pass lint, pass typecheck, and silently win over yours.** Your own
452	  action just does nothing, on your machine only. Full table, plus the real key
453	  combinations behind every `Keyboard.Shortcut.Common.*` (`Remove` is `⌃X`, not
454	  `⌘⌫`; `Duplicate` is `⌘D`, not `⌘⇧D`), in
455	  `references/ui-patterns.md` → *Shortcuts Raycast has already taken*.
456	- **`@raycast/api` bundles its own copy of `@types/react`.** Type props that hold
457	  JSX as `React.JSX.Element`, not `React.ReactNode` — the root `ReactNode` is a
458	  structurally different type that silently fails to match `ActionPanel`'s
459	  children.
460	- **`ray lint` runs MORE checks when it thinks it is in CI.** Locally it prints
461	  five steps; with `CI=true` it prints seven — `validate package-lock.json` and
462	  `validate other lock files` appear only there, and nothing announces the
463	  difference. Your local gate is a *subset* of the remote one, which is backwards.
464	  Put `CI=true` in the lint recipe so they cannot diverge. The check that bites:
465	  every `resolved` URL in the lockfile must be `registry.npmjs.org`, so a global
466	  npm registry pointing at a mirror (`registry.npmmirror.com`, an internal
467	  Artifactory) writes a lockfile the store rejects. Fix by host substitution —
468	  the tarballs are identical, so `integrity` stays valid, and
469	  `npm install --package-lock-only --registry=…` will *not* rewrite URLs already
470	  in the file.
471	- **`@types/node` must match Raycast's runtime (Node 22), not your shell's node.**
472	  Typing against 24 lets you write APIs that compile and throw at runtime.
473	- **Never `shell: true`.** Use `execFile` with an argv array. And raise
474	  `maxBuffer` — the 1 MB default truncates a large JSON read into a confusing
475	  parse error instead of a clear failure.
476	- **Global flags of clap-based CLIs must precede the subcommand.** `foo status
477	  --color never` exits **2** with a clap error; `foo --color never status` is
478	  correct. Exit codes are 0/1/2, not 0/1. Assert your generated argv against the
479	  CLI's own `--help` at verify time so a misplaced flag fails in the gate.
480	- **There is no test runner in a Raycast extension, and adding one is store-review
481	  noise.** Keep pure modules free of `@raycast/api` imports and assert them from
482	  one `dev-check.ts`, compiled by the already-installed `tsc` and run under
483	  `node`. That import discipline is the entire precondition — a barrel that pulls
484	  in the transport pulls in `@raycast/api` with it.
485	- **A `mode: "no-view"` command exports `async function Command(props)`, not a
486	  React component.** There is no window, so feedback is `showHUD`.
487	- **`ray lint` passes with a completely empty `metadata/`.** Screenshots, icon
488	  dimensions, the CHANGELOG placeholder, and a registered `author` are review-time
489	  requirements it never checks.
490	- **The extension IS the repo root, and `ray publish` copies the directory
491	  verbatim** — not the git index. Ignored-but-present directories ride along into
492	  the review PR. Export an allowlisted subset if that matters.
493	- **Fence untrusted program output in markdown**, and neutralise embedded
494	  backticks with a zero-width space. A build log full of `#` otherwise renders as
495	  headings, and a fence inside the output closes yours early.
496	- **`launchCommand` + `launchContext` is the supported cross-command path**, but
497	  push a view only once (guard with a ref — the receiving command re-renders on
498	  every poll) and wait for dependent async state before acting on the context.
499	  Acting early opens the previous account's data and looks like it worked.
500	- **A deeplink triggered from outside Raycast prompts for confirmation.**
501	  `launchCommand` from inside does not. So an external nudge is a poor substitute,
502	  and some verification genuinely needs a keypress rather than a URL.
503
```

19	## Top level
20	
21	```json
22	{
23	  "$schema": "https://www.raycast.com/schemas/extension.json",
24	  "name": "my-ext",
25	  "title": "My Extension",
26	  "description": "One sentence. This is what the store shows.",
27	  "icon": "extension-icon.png",
28	  "author": "your_raycast_username",
29	  "license": "MIT",
30	  "categories": ["Developer Tools", "Productivity"],
31	  "platforms": ["macOS"],
32	  "commands": [],
33	  "preferences": []
34	}
35	```
36	
37	- `name` is the store slug and must be kebab-case. `title` is what users see.
38	- `author` must be your **registered Raycast username**, not your name.
39	- `icon` resolves relative to `assets/`.
40	- **`platforms: ["macOS"]` is mandatory when any command is `menu-bar`** — that
41	  mode does not exist elsewhere.
42	- **There is no `version` field** for a store extension. The store derives it.
43	- `$schema` gives you completion in an editor and is what `ray lint` validates
44	  against.
45	
46	### String length minimums
47	
48	The schema enforces minimums that are easy to trip and whose error message
49	(`must NOT have fewer than N characters`) **does not name the field** — you get a
50	line number and have to count. Read straight from
51	<https://www.raycast.com/schemas/extension.json>:
52	
53	| Field | min | max |
54	| --- | ---: | ---: |
55	| `name` | 3 | 255 |
56	| `title` | 2 | 255 |
57	| `description` | **16** | 2048 |
58	| `author`, `owner`, `contributors[]` | 2 | 75 |
59	| `keywords[]` | 1 | 25 |
60	| `commands[].name` / `.title` / `.subtitle` | 2 | 255 |
61	| `commands[].description` | **12** | 2048 |
62	| `preferences[].name` | 2 | 255 |
63	| `preferences[].description` | **8** | 1024 |
64	| `preferences[].title` | 2 (0 for a checkbox) | 255 |
65	| `preferences[].label` (checkbox) | 1 | 255 |
66	| `arguments[].name` | 2 | 255 |
67	| `arguments[].placeholder` | 1 | 255 |
68	| `tools[].name` | 2 | 64 |
69	| `tools[].description` | **12** | 2048 |
70	
71	"Tasks." is 6 characters and will be rejected. Write a sentence.
72	
73	## commands[]
74	
75	```json
76	{
77	  "name": "tasks",
78	  "title": "Tasks",
79	  "subtitle": "My Extension",
80	  "description": "Browse and act on the queue.",
81	  "mode": "view",
82	  "interval": "1m",
83	  "arguments": [],
84	  "preferences": []
85	}
86	```
87	
88	**`commands[].name` must equal the filename**: `"name": "tasks"` requires
89	`src/tasks.tsx`. A mismatch is a build error with a message that does not say so
90	clearly.
91	
92	Modes, and what each implies:
93	
94	- **`view`** — default-exports a React component. Pushes onto the navigation
95	  stack. `useNavigation()` gives `push`/`pop`.
96	- **`no-view`** — default-exports `async function Command(props)`. **Not a
97	  component.** There is no window, so `showToast` degrades to a HUD; call
98	  `showHUD` directly to make that explicit. This is often the highest
99	  value-per-line command in an extension: an argument, a return, done.
100	- **`menu-bar`** — returns a `MenuBarExtra`. See `menu-bar.md`. `interval` is
101	  valid only here and is manifest-only: a preference cannot change it, because
102	  Raycast renders its own refresh control in the command's settings. Use `"1m"`.
103	
104	Per-command `preferences` and `arguments` are scoped to that command and appear
105	in its own settings pane. Extension-level ones live at the top level and apply to
106	everything.
107	
108	## arguments[]
109	
110	Arguments are the escape hatch from ever opening the UI:
111	
112	```json
113	"arguments": [
114	  { "name": "query", "type": "text", "placeholder": "status=failed", "required": false },
115	  { "name": "target", "type": "dropdown", "data": [{ "title": "Local", "value": "local" }] }
116	]
117	```
118	
119	They are typed into root search before the command runs, and arrive as
120	`props.arguments`. A power user filtering a list should never have to open it.
121	Types: `text`, `password`, `dropdown`.
122	
123	## preferences[]
124	
125	```json
126	{
127	  "name": "binaryPath",
128	  "type": "textfield",
129	  "required": false,
130	  "title": "Binary Path",
131	  "description": "Absolute path. Raycast runs under launchd with no shell rc, so a bare name is never on PATH.",
132	  "placeholder": "/opt/homebrew/bin/mytool"
133	}
134	```
135	
136	**The allowed `type` values are exactly:**
137	
138	```text
139	appPicker | checkbox | dropdown | password | textfield | file | directory
140	```
141	
142	**There is no multi-line type.** `"type": "textarea"` fails `ray lint` with
143	`must be equal to one of the allowed values`. `Form.TextArea` is a *form*
144	component inside a command and has nothing to do with `preferences[]`.
145	
146	This bites in a way that produces no error at all: a preference documented as
147	"one entry per line" parses fine, its unit assertions pass, and it accepts
148	exactly one entry forever — because a `textfield` renders as a single-line input
149	and the user cannot type a newline. If you need a list, pick a single-line
150	separator (`;` between records, `|` between fields), accept newlines too in the
151	parser for values set by other means, and **say in the docs why the separator is
152	what it is** — otherwise a reader assumes it is arbitrary taste and reaches for a
153	newline.
154	
155	Conventions that pay off:
156	
157	- **A checkbox needs both `title` and `label`.** `title` is the row heading,
158	  `label` is the text beside the box.
159	- **A dropdown uses `data: [{ title, value }]`**, and its values become a string
160	  union in the generated types. Switch on that union rather than on `string`.
161	- **Put the trap in the description.** "Higher values cost one extra call per
162	  selection change." "Keeps a large queue from rendering hundreds of menu items
163	  every minute." The description is the only documentation most users read.
164	- **Surface invalid input rather than dropping it.** A malformed line that
165	  silently vanishes is indistinguishable from the feature being broken.
166	
167	## The generated types
168	
169	`ray build` writes `raycast-env.d.ts` with global namespaces derived from the
170	manifest, and **fields are typed as required**:
171	
172	```ts
173	declare namespace Preferences {
174	  type Tasks = ExtensionPreferences & { showDetail: boolean; detailLogLines: string };
175	}
176	declare namespace Arguments {
177	  type Tasks = { query: string };
178	}
179	```
180	
181	Consume them:
182	
183	```ts
184	const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.Tasks>();
185	export default function Command(props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.Tasks }>) {}
186	```
187	
188	**Never hand-write a `Preferences` interface.** The whole value of the generated
189	file is that a manifest change which your code does not follow becomes a *compile
190	error*. A hand-written copy silently drifts, and a code default that disagrees
191	with the manifest default is a bug nobody ever finds.
192	
193	Commit `raycast-env.d.ts`, list it in `tsconfig.json`'s `include`, and regenerate
194	with `npm run build` after every manifest edit.
195	
196	Note that numeric preferences arrive as **strings** — a `textfield` is text.
197	`Number(prefs.detailLogLines) || 20`.
198	
199	## Cross-command launching
200	
201	```ts
202	import { launchCommand, LaunchType } from "@raycast/api";
203	
204	await launchCommand({
205	  name: "queue-menu",
206	  type: LaunchType.Background,          // refresh a sibling without showing it
207	  context: { group: "archive" },
208	}).catch(() => {});                      // the target may be disabled by the user
209	```
210	
211	The receiving command reads `props.launchContext`. Three rules, all learned by
212	observation rather than from the docs:
213	
214	- **Always `.catch(() => {})`.** The target command can be disabled, and an
215	  unhandled rejection in a background launch is silent but real.
216	- **Push a view at most once.** The receiving command re-renders on every poll;
217	  without a `useRef` guard you stack duplicate views on the navigation stack.
218	
219	  ```ts
220	  const pushed = useRef(false);
221	  useEffect(() => {
222	    if (pushed.current || !ctx?.logTaskId) return;
223	    pushed.current = true;
224	    push(<LogView id={ctx.logTaskId} />);
225	  }, [ctx?.logTaskId]);
226	  ```
227	
228	- **Wait for dependent async state before acting on context.** If ids are
229	  per-account and the account selection is restored asynchronously, acting on the
230	  context immediately opens the *previous* account's data — which looks like it
231	  worked and shows someone else's record with the same id. Gate on the
232	  dependency:
233	
234	  ```ts
235	  if (ctx.accountName && current.name !== ctx.accountName) return;
236	  ```
237	
238	- **Context should win over remembered state.** If a command launches a sibling
239	  with an explicit filter, that filter must override the sibling's persisted
240	  choice, or "Show X in Group" silently shows a different group.
241	
242	Also useful: `updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle })` rewrites *this* command's
243	subtitle in root search. Call it from a fetch's `onData`, and `.catch(() => {})`.
244	
245	## Deeplinks
246	
247	`open "raycast://extensions/<author>/<extension>/<command>"` opens a command from
248	outside Raycast — and shows a confirmation first:
249	
250	> **Request to open ‹Command›** — The command was triggered from outside of
251	> Raycast.
252	
253	Trust is per-command. Two consequences: an external nudge is a poor substitute
254	for `launchCommand` (which does not prompt), and some verification during
255	development genuinely needs a real keypress rather than a URL. A deeplink is
256	still the right tool for scripting a sequence of commands you are about to
257	screenshot.
258	
259	## AI tools
260	
261	```json
262	"tools": [{ "name": "list-tasks", "title": "List Tasks", "description": "…" }]
263	```
264	
265	- **Raycast AI is Pro-gated**, so tools can never be the primary UX of an
266	  extension. Ship the commands first.
267	- Tools do not appear in root search. Raycast AI selects them by `description`,
268	  so the description is prompt engineering, not documentation.
269	- **There is no confirmation surface inside a tool call** comparable to
270	  `confirmAlert`. A first version must be read-only. Anything destructive needs a
271	  design for consent that does not exist yet in the tool API.
272	- If your transport already returns structured data, a tool is a thin wrapper —
273	  the work is prompt-shaped, not code-shaped.
274
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Publishing to the Raycast Store
2	
3	Read this when the user asks to publish, submit, or "make this store-ready", or
4	when `check-store-readiness.sh` reports a failure you want the reasoning behind.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	- [What publishing actually is](#what-publishing-actually-is)
9	- [The checklist](#the-checklist)
10	- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
11	- [What ray lint does and does not check](#what-ray-lint-does-and-does-not-check)
12	- [The CHANGELOG placeholder](#the-changelog-placeholder)
13	- [Requiring an external binary](#requiring-an-external-binary)
14	- [What rides along](#what-rides-along)
15	- [What cannot be automated](#what-cannot-be-automated)
16	
17	---
18	
19	## What publishing actually is
20	
21	`npx @raycast/api@latest publish` authenticates with GitHub and opens a **pull
22	request against `raycast/extensions`**. CI runs on the PR, then a human from the
23	Raycast team reviews it. Turnaround is days, not seconds.
24	
25	This is closer to Homebrew core than to npm. Treat submission as a one-way door:
26	the readiness checks below are the validation step, and the publish command is
27	something the user types, not something a script fires.
28	
29	`ray publish` has no `--dry-run`, no `--yes`, and no path argument. Its
30	`-I/--non-interactive` flag only suppresses interactive *output*; it does not
31	supply credentials or answers.
32	
33	## The checklist
34	
35	```text
36	[ ] author is your REGISTERED Raycast username (not your display name)
37	[ ] license: "MIT" in package.json AND an MIT LICENSE file at the root
38	[ ] at least one category, Title Case, from Raycast's list
39	[ ] platforms: ["macOS"] if any command is mode: "menu-bar"
40	[ ] a one-sentence description — this is what the store shows
41	[ ] package-lock.json committed; npm ci must work from a clean checkout
42	[ ] assets/extension-icon.png at exactly 512x512, readable on light AND dark
43	[ ] a separate monochrome template SVG for any menu-bar icon
44	[ ] CHANGELOG.md opening with `## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}`
45	[ ] README.md covering setup, external requirements, and any default that
46	    makes a fresh install look broken
47	[ ] 3-6 PNGs at exactly 2000x1250 in metadata/
48	[ ] no `version` field in package.json — the store derives it
49	[ ] no Keychain access (extensions requesting it are rejected)
50	[ ] tsc --noEmit clean, ray lint clean, ray build -e dist clean
51	```
52	
53	Note the last one. `ray build` defaults to `-e dev`; `npm run build` is usually
54	bare `ray build`, so **the distribution build may never have been run**. Run
55	`ray build -e dist` at least once before submitting — and note it is a stronger
56	check than the dev build: it shells out to `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, so it
57	fails on type errors the dev build cheerfully bundles.
58	
59	Naming follows the Apple Style Guide: Title Case for extension and command
60	titles, US English throughout, specific rather than generic names.
61	
62	## Screenshots
63	
64	Spec: **3–6 PNGs, exactly 2000×1250 (16:10)**, in `metadata/`. No dark-mode
65	variants — one set only.
66	
67	The supported capture path is Raycast's **Window Capture**:
68	
69	1. Give it a hotkey: Raycast Settings → Advanced → Window Capture, or bind the
70	   **Capture Window** command.

```

Conditional rows are `{cond ? <Row/> : null}` — an undefined `text` renders an
empty row rather than nothing.

A standalone `<Detail>` takes `isLoading`, `navigationTitle`, `markdown`,
`metadata`, and `actions`, and is the right surface for a full error page or a
log view.

## ActionPanel and shortcuts

```tsx
<ActionPanel>
  <ActionPanel.Section>
    <Action.Push title="Show Log" target={<LogView id={t.id} />} />
    <Action title="Kill" style={Action.Style.Destructive}
            shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"], key: "k" }} onAction={kill} />
  </ActionPanel.Section>
  <ActionPanel.Section title="Copy">
    <Action.CopyToClipboard content={t.command} shortcut={Keyboard.Shortcut.Common.Copy} />
  </ActionPanel.Section>
</ActionPanel>
```

- The **first action is the ⏎ action.** Order matters more than any other UI
  decision in the panel.
- Prefer `Keyboard.Shortcut.Common.*` so bindings match the rest of Raycast —
  and read the table below before writing one into a README, because their key
  combinations are not what the names suggest.
- **Name a shortcut after what it does, not after its family.** If you have two
  restarts, one destructive and one not, `⌘⇧R` and `⌘⌥R` need to be documented by
  behaviour or someone will lose work.
- `ActionPanel.Submenu` for a set of alternatives (accounts, groups) that would
  otherwise flood the panel.

### Shortcuts Raycast has already taken

Three separate sets, and only the first is enforced by anything.

**1. Reserved globally — `ray lint` fails the build.**

| Key | Raycast's use |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘K` | Open Action Panel |
| `⌘P` | Open Search Bar Dropdown |

Bind these and they are silently ignored at runtime; nothing throws. `ray lint`
is the only thing that catches it, which is one of the reasons `lint` belongs in
the gate alongside `tsc`.

**2. The Debug section — injected into *every* action panel while an extension
is in development, and NOT caught by `ray lint`.**

| Key | Raycast's use |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘R` | Reload |
| `⇧⌘S` | Open Support Directory |
| `⇧⌘D` | Open Documentation |
| `⇧⌘X` | Clear Assets Cache |
| `⌘⌥D` | Open React Developer Tools |

These are the dangerous ones. They pass lint, they pass typecheck, and a store
user never sees the conflict — but **you** develop against it, so your own
action does nothing and looks broken for reasons that have nothing to do with
your code. A detail-pane toggle on `⇧⌘D` was dead for exactly this reason and
took a screenshot to diagnose.

# Bring `raycast-extension-dev` up to date: cross-platform + AI Extensions

## Context

`skills/local/raycast-extension-dev` was written against a macOS-only, Pro-gated
picture of Raycast that is no longer true. Two independent gaps:

1. **Cross-platform.** Raycast for Windows shipped, and `platforms` landed in the
   manifest in **1.103.0 (2025-09-15)**. The skill declares itself macOS-only in
   its opening paragraph (`SKILL.md:18-19`) and hardcodes `platforms: ["macOS"]`
   in the scaffolder template, the store checklist, and the readiness script — so
   every extension it produces is silently Windows-invisible, and it teaches none
   of the per-platform mechanisms (shortcuts, preference defaults, `windowsAppId`,
   `runPowerShellScript`).

2. **AI Extensions.** The skill tells the agent to *deprioritise* AI tools on two
   grounds, one of which is **factually wrong**:
   - `SKILL.md:45-46` / `manifest-and-commands.md:268-270`: *"there is no
     `confirmAlert` equivalent inside a tool call, so a first version must be
     read-only."* — `Tool.Confirmation<Input>` exists and is documented.
   - *"Pro-gated, so they can never be the primary UX"* — access also comes from
     the free message allowance, Custom Providers (`providers.yaml`, e.g. GitHub
     Copilot) and local Ollama models. The docs page still says Pro; reality has
     moved. The only correct rule is the runtime gate `environment.canAccess(AI)`.
   - `ai.instructions` / `ai.evals` / `ai.yaml` / `npx ray evals` are absent
     entirely — and `ai.evals` is what renders the **Suggested Prompts** list
     under `@extension` in Quick AI.

Outcome: an agent using this skill should treat macOS as a *default*, not a
premise; should reach for `platforms: ["macOS", "Windows"]` whenever nothing
platform-specific is used; and should propose an AI tool layer (with confirmation
and suggested prompts) for any extension whose transport already returns
structured data.

## Verified facts — the source of truth for this rewrite

All confirmed against live docs on 2026-07-28. **Do not re-derive from memory.**

### Cross-platform

| Fact | Source wording |
|---|---|
| `platforms` values | `"macOS"` or `"Windows"` |
| Default when omitted | *"By default, if not specified, the field's value is `["macOS"]`"* (changelog 1.103.0, 2025-09-15) |
| Scope | **extension-level only** — no per-command `platforms` |
| Per-platform values | *"you can specify a different value per platform by passing an object: `{ "macOS": ..., "Windows": ... }`"* — applies to preference `default` |
| Per-platform shortcuts | changelog **1.98.0 (2025-05-08)**; `{ macOS: { modifiers: ["cmd","shift"], key: "c" }, Windows: { modifiers: ["ctrl","shift"], key: "c" } }` |
| Hardcoded modifier | *"If you use shortcuts and specify a modifier like `cmd`, the shortcut will be ignored on Windows (and vice-versa…)"* — **silent**, no lint error |
| Menu bar | *"Menubar commands aren't available on Windows."* |
| Scripts | `runPowerShellScript` — *"Only available on Windows"*; `runAppleScript` is macOS-only |
| Applications | `Application` carries both `bundleId` (*"The macOS bundle identifier"*) and `windowsAppId` (*"The Windows App ID"*) |
| Store guidance | *"if you use platform-specific APIs, restrict the `platforms` field to the corresponding platform"* |
| Porting | *"All extensions that do not require native code will work out of the box on both platforms."* (raycast.com/windows) |
| Requirements | Raycast ≥ 1.26.0, Node ≥ 22.14, npm ≥ 7; Windows 10 21H2+ / Windows 11 |

**Undocumented — write as unverified, do not assert:** whether AI Extensions,
Browser Extension API, or Window Management API work on Windows. Neither the
changelog nor raycast.com/windows lists them as unavailable.

### AI Extensions

| Fact | Source wording |
|---|---|
| `tools[]` fields | `name` (*"directly maps to the entry point file"*), `title`, `description`, `icon` |
| Tool signature | *"A tool expects a single object as its input"*; `export default function tool(input: Input)` |
| Parameter schema | JSDoc on the `Input` type — *"add descriptions as JSDoc comments"* |
| Confirmation | `type Confirmation<T> = (input: T) => Promise<undefined \| {...}>`; `export const confirmation: Tool.Confirmation<Input> = (input) => {`; returns `message`, `info[]` (`{name, value}`), `style` (regular/destructive), `image`; `undefined` skips it; *"called before the actual tool is executed"* |
| `ai.instructions` | *"added as a system message whenever the extension is mentioned"* |
| `ai.evals` | *"Evals are a way to test your AI extension. Think of them as integrations tests."* |
| **Suggested Prompts** | *"They are also used as suggested prompts for the user to learn how to make the most out of your AI Extension."* — `usedAsExample` defaults to `true` |
| File location | *"we recommend you to use a `ai.yaml` file in the root of your extension next to the `package.json`"* |
| Runner | `npx ray evals`; matcher shown: `callsTool` |
| Access gate | *"You can check if a user has access to the API using `environment.canAccess(AI)`"* / *"If the user doesn't wish to get access, the API call will throw an error."* |
| Stale doc to cite as stale | ai/getting-started: *"To use AI APIs or AI Extensions, you need to subscribe to Raycast Pro."* — contradicted by the free allowance, Custom Providers and Ollama Local Models in Raycast Settings → AI |

## Approved Plan:
# Bring `raycast-extension-dev` up to date: cross-platform + AI Extensions

## Context

`skills/local/raycast-extension-dev` was written against a macOS-only, Pro-gated
picture of Raycast that is no longer true. Two independent gaps:

1. **Cross-platform.** Raycast for Windows shipped, and `platforms` landed in the
   manifest in **1.103.0 (2025-09-15)**. The skill declares itself macOS-only in
   its opening paragraph (`SKILL.md:18-19`) and hardcodes `platforms: ["macOS"]`
   in the scaffolder template, the store checklist, and the readiness script — so
   every extension it produces is silently Windows-invisible, and it teaches none
   of the per-platform mechanisms (shortcuts, preference defaults, `windowsAppId`,
   `runPowerShellScript`).

2. **AI Extensions.** The skill tells the agent to *deprioritise* AI tools on two
   grounds, one of which is **factually wrong**:
   - `SKILL.md:45-46` / `manifest-and-commands.md:268-270`: *"there is no
     `confirmAlert` equivalent inside a tool call, so a first version must be
     read-only."* — `Tool.Confirmation<Input>` exists and is documented.
   - *"Pro-gated, so they can never be the primary UX"* — access also comes from
     the free message allowance, Custom Providers (`providers.yaml`, e.g. GitHub
     Copilot) and local Ollama models. The docs page still says Pro; reality has
     moved. The only correct rule is the runtime gate `environment.canAccess(AI)`.
   - `ai.instructions` / `ai.evals` / `ai.yaml` / `npx ray evals` are absent
     entirely — and `ai.evals` is what renders the **Suggested Prompts** list
     under `@extension` in Quick AI.

Outcome: an agent using this skill should treat macOS as a *default*, not a
premise; should reach for `platforms: ["macOS", "Windows"]` whenever nothing
platform-specific is used; and should propose an AI tool layer (with confirmation
and suggested prompts) for any extension whose transport already returns
structured data.

## Verified facts — the source of truth for this rewrite

All confirmed against live docs on 2026-07-28. **Do not re-derive from memory.**

### Cross-platform

| Fact | Source wording |
|---|---|
| `platforms` values | `"macOS"` or `"Windows"` |
| Default when omitted | *"By default, if not specified, the field's value is `["macOS"]`"* (changelog 1.103.0, 2025-09-15) |
| Scope | **extension-level only** — no per-command `platforms` |
| Per-platform values | *"you can specify a different value per platform by passing an object: `{ "macOS": ..., "Windows": ... }`"* — applies to preference `default` |
| Per-platform shortcuts | changelog **1.98.0 (2025-05-08)**; `{ macOS: { modifiers: ["cmd","shift"], key: "c" }, Windows: { modifiers: ["ctrl","shift"], key: "c" } }` |
| Hardcoded modifier | *"If you use shortcuts and specify a modifier like `cmd`, the shortcut will be ignored on Windows (and vice-versa…)"* — **silent**, no lint error |
| Menu bar | *"Menubar commands aren't available on Windows."* |
| Scripts | `runPowerShellScript` — *"Only available on Windows"*; `runAppleScript` is macOS-only |
| Applications | `Application` carries both `bundleId` (*"The macOS bundle identifier"*) and `windowsAppId` (*"The Windows App ID"*) |
| Store guidance | *"if you use platform-specific APIs, restrict the `platforms` field to the corresponding platform"* |
| Porting | *"All extensions that do not require native code will work out of the box on both platforms."* (raycast.com/windows) |
| Requirements | Raycast ≥ 1.26.0, Node ≥ 22.14, npm ≥ 7; Windows 10 21H2+ / Windows 11 |

**Undocumented — write as unverified, do not assert:** whether AI Extensions,
Browser Extension API, or Window Management API work on Windows. Neither the
changelog nor raycast.com/windows lists them as unavailable.

### AI Extensions

| `ai.instructions` | *"added as a system message whenever the extension is mentioned"* |

1	# Runtime and subprocesses
2	
3	Read this when the extension shells out to a binary, resolves a path, spawns or
4	streams a subprocess, or reports `spawn … ENOENT` / "works in my terminal but not
5	from Raycast".
6	
7	## Table of contents
8	
9	- [The launchd environment](#the-launchd-environment)
10	- [Resolving a binary](#resolving-a-binary)
11	- [The corollary: never start a daemon from Raycast](#the-corollary-never-start-a-daemon-from-raycast)
12	- [Running a command](#running-a-command)
13	- [Streaming output](#streaming-output)
14	- [An error taxonomy](#an-error-taxonomy)
15	- [Argv discipline](#argv-discipline)
16	- [Node version](#node-version)
17	
18	---

20	## The launchd environment
21	
22	Raycast runs extensions in a managed Node process started by **launchd**. launchd
23	never sources `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.bash_profile`, or any other shell rc,
24	because those are read by an interactive shell and there is no shell here.
25	
26	Every `PATH` entry you rely on — `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`,
27	`~/.local/bin`, a mise or asdf shim directory — is added *by those files*. The
28	extension's `PATH` is roughly:
29	
30	```text
31	/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
32	```
33	
34	So `execFile("pueue", …)` fails with `Error: spawn pueue ENOENT` while
35	`which pueue` in your terminal answers instantly.
36	
37	**The dev console lies.** `ray develop` runs in the terminal you launched it
38	from, and inherits that terminal's full interactive environment. A resolver that
39	would fail in production passes there every time. Any change touching `PATH`,
40	`HOME`, or a config-file location must be exercised by opening the command **from
41	Raycast root search or the menu bar**, not from the dev console.
42	
43	You can see the real environment by having a command render
44	`JSON.stringify(process.env, null, 2)` once, opened from root search. Do it once
45	per project — it takes a minute and settles every argument.
46	
47	## Resolving a binary
48	
49	Never invoke a bare name. Resolve an absolute path, in this order:
50	
51	```ts
52	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
53	import { homedir } from "node:os";
54	import { join } from "node:path";
55	
56	const PROBE_DIRS = [
57	  "/opt/homebrew/bin",            // Apple Silicon Homebrew
58	  "/usr/local/bin",               // Intel Homebrew — and Rosetta, and MacPorts-adjacent
59	  join(homedir(), ".cargo", "bin"),
60	  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
```
</details></tool-use>

# Cross-platform: macOS and Windows

Read this when targeting Windows, when a shortcut does nothing on one OS, when
shelling out to a platform-specific script, or when an extension you can install
on your Mac does not appear in the Windows store.

## Table of contents

- [The platforms field](#the-platforms-field)
- [What actually differs](#what-actually-differs)
- [The three layers](#the-three-layers)
- [Scripts: AppleScript and PowerShell](#scripts-applescript-and-powershell)
- [Shortcuts](#shortcuts)
- [Per-platform manifest values](#per-platform-manifest-values)
- [Applications and paths](#applications-and-paths)
- [Which existing gotchas are macOS-only](#which-existing-gotchas-are-macos-only)
- [Developing on Windows](#developing-on-windows)

---

## The platforms field

`platforms` arrived in **1.103.0 (2025-09-15)**. It is the field that makes an
extension visible on Windows:

\```json
"platforms": ["macOS", "Windows"]
\```

Three facts that decide everything else:

- **The default is `["macOS"]`.** Verbatim from the changelog: *"By default, if
  not specified, the field's value is `["macOS"]`."* So omitting the field is not
  neutral — it is a choice, and it is the choice that hides a perfectly portable
  extension from every Windows user. A large share of the store is Windows-capable
  code that was simply never declared.
- **It is extension-level. There is no per-command `platforms`.** One
  `mode: "menu-bar"` command therefore pins the *entire* extension to macOS,
  including the six view commands next to it. If you want both, the menu bar has
  to move to a separate extension.
- **The store shows only what matches the current OS.** There is no "unavailable
  on your platform" row, so a wrong `platforms` value looks exactly like the
  extension not existing.

The store guidance is the inverse framing, and it is the rule to follow:
*"if you use platform-specific APIs, restrict the `platforms` field to the
corresponding platform"*. Declare both, then subtract.

## What actually differs

Raycast renders the UI. You ship React, TypeScript, and Node — none of which
cares about the OS. From raycast.com/windows: *"All extensions that do not
require native code will work out of the box on both platforms."*

| Surface | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `List` / `Detail` / `Form` / `ActionPanel` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `useCachedPromise`, `Cache`, `LocalStorage` | ✅ | ✅ |
| REST/GraphQL, any pure-JS npm package | ✅ | ✅ |
| `execFile` of a bundled or user-installed binary | ✅ | ✅ (different path shape) |
| `mode: "menu-bar"` / `MenuBarExtra` | ✅ | ❌ *"Menubar commands aren't available on Windows."* |
| `runAppleScript` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `runPowerShellScript` | ❌ | ✅ *"Only available on Windows"* |
| `Application.bundleId` | ✅ | — use `windowsAppId` |
| AI Extensions (`tools[]`) | ✅ | **undocumented** |
| Browser Extension API | ✅ | **undocumented** |
| Window Management API | ✅ | **undocumented** |

The last three rows are honest gaps, not omissions. Neither the changelog nor
raycast.com/windows states whether those APIs work on Windows. **Do not assert
either way** — verify on a Windows install before declaring `Windows` for an
extension that depends on them.

One trap worth naming: Raycast for Windows *has* window management as a built-in
feature. That says nothing about whether the `WindowManagement` API is exposed to
third-party extensions there. A shipped feature is not a shipped API.

## The three layers

Design for the split before you need it. Only the bottom layer is ever
platform-aware:

\```text
Raycast UI          List / Detail / Form / ActionPanel     100% shared
Domain logic        parsing, models, argv builders          ~100% shared
OS adapter          AppleScript / PowerShell, paths         split
\```

\```text
src/
├── tasks.tsx              UI — imports from platform/, never branches itself
├── lib/
│   ├── transport.ts       the Mutation data-union seam (see SKILL.md Workflow B)
│   └── platform/
│       ├── index.ts       picks an implementation once, at import time
│       ├── macos.ts       runAppleScript, bundleId, /opt/homebrew probing
│       └── windows.ts     runPowerShellScript, windowsAppId, %LOCALAPPDATA%
\```

\```ts
// lib/platform/index.ts
import * as macos from "./macos";
import * as windows from "./windows";

export const platform = process.platform === "win32" ? windows : macos;
\```

**Branch once, at the seam — never in a component.** A `process.platform` check
inside a render function is a bug in waiting: it makes every surface responsible
for knowing the OS, and it defeats the point of the transport seam, which is that
the UI does not know how anything is fetched.

Realistic sharing, by extension shape:

| Shape | Shared |
| --- | --- |
| SaaS / REST API wrapper | ~100% — usually just declare `Windows` and test |
| Local CLI wrapper | 70–90% — binary resolution and paths differ, argv does not |
| Deep OS automation | 30–70% |
| Menu bar, Finder, AppleScript-first | macOS only, or a genuine second implementation |

## Scripts: AppleScript and PowerShell

\```ts
import { runAppleScript, runPowerShellScript } from "@raycast/utils";
\```

Both live in `@raycast/utils`, and each throws on the wrong OS —
`runPowerShellScript` is documented *"Only available on Windows"*. Importing both
in one module is fine; **calling** the wrong one is not. Keep each behind its own
file so the platform picker decides, and so a reader can see at a glance which
half of the behaviour they are reading.

Nothing checks this. `ray lint` will not tell you that a `platforms` list
including `Windows` sits above a `runAppleScript` call —
`scripts/check-store-readiness.sh` will (`platforms-windows-macos-apis`).

## Shortcuts

Per-platform shortcuts landed in **1.98.0 (2025-05-08)**:

\```ts
shortcut={{
  macOS:   { modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"],  key: "c" },
  Windows: { modifiers: ["ctrl", "shift"], key: "c" },
}}
\```

**A hardcoded modifier is dropped in silence.** Verbatim: *"If you use shortcuts
and specify a modifier like `cmd`, the shortcut will be ignored on Windows (and
vice-versa, if you specify a modifier like `windows`, it won't be available on
macOS)."* No error, no lint failure, no runtime warning — the action is simply
there with no key beside it, and the bug report says "the shortcut doesn't work".

The cheap way to never hit this: **prefer `Keyboard.Shortcut.Common.*`**, which
Raycast maps per platform itself. Reach for a literal modifier object only when
no common constant fits, and then write both branches in the same expression so
neither can be forgotten later.

## Per-platform manifest values

The manifest accepts a platform-keyed object anywhere a plain value is allowed —
*"you can specify a different value per platform by passing an object:
`{ "macOS": ..., "Windows": ... }`"*. The case that matters is a preference
default that is a filesystem path:

\```json
{
  "name": "workspacePath",
  "type": "directory",
  "title": "Workspace",
  "description": "Where projects are scanned from.",
  "default": {
    "macOS": "/Users/me/projects",
    "Windows": "C:\\Users\\me\\projects"
  }
}
\```

Note the doubled backslashes — this is JSON, and a single `\U` is an invalid
escape that fails to parse before `ray lint` ever sees the schema.

Do not hand a user a default that cannot exist on their machine. A `textfield`
holding `/opt/homebrew/bin/mytool` on Windows is not a harmless leftover: it
passes validation, fails `existsSync`, and the extension reports "binary not
found" while pointing at a path that was never plausible.

## Applications and paths

`Application` carries an identifier for each platform:

\```ts
interface Application {
  name: string;
  path: string;
  bundleId?: string;       // "The macOS bundle identifier", e.g. com.raycast.macos
  windowsAppId?: string;   // "The Windows App ID"
  localizedName?: string;
}
\```

\```text
macOS    /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app          bundleId com.microsoft.VSCode
Windows  C:\Users\…\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe
\```

Both fields are optional, so **match on the one for the current platform and fall
back to `name`** rather than assuming either is populated. And build every path
with `node:path` — `join`, `sep`, `homedir()` — never a string literal with a
separator in it.

## Which existing gotchas are macOS-only

Several hard-won rules elsewhere in this skill are macOS-shaped. They are still
correct; they are just scoped:

| Rule | Scope | Windows equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| launchd strips `PATH` to `/usr/bin:/bin` | macOS | Raycast on Windows likewise does not run your shell profile — resolve absolute paths there too, from Windows locations |
| Probe `/opt/homebrew/bin` **and** `/usr/local/bin` | macOS | probe `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, `%ProgramFiles%`, and a user-set preference |
| `sips` for icon dimensions | macOS | `check-store-readiness.sh` reports `skip`, which is **not** a pass |
| Monochrome template SVG tinted by the menu bar | macOS | no menu bar, so no equivalent |

The invariant that survives both platforms: **never invoke a bare binary name,
and let a preference override the resolved path.** The reason differs by OS; the
rule does not.

## Developing on Windows

Requirements are the same toolchain, one host apart: **Raycast ≥ 1.26.0,
Node ≥ 22.14, npm ≥ 7**, on **Windows 10 21H2+ or Windows 11**. `Create
Extension`, `Import Extension`, and `Fork Extension` all exist there, and
`npm run dev` hot-reloads the same way.

What does not carry over is this skill's `Justfile.template` gate as written —
`just` runs fine on Windows, but the recipes assume a POSIX shell. On a
Windows-only checkout, run the four stages directly:

\```powershell
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
npx ray lint
npx ray build
\```

If you develop on macOS and declare `Windows`, you have shipped something you
have not run. That is a defensible choice for a pure API extension and a bad one
for anything that touches the filesystem — say which in the PR.
